title: Policy-driven capacity contracts and observable burst accountant
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Dedicated customers have asked for first-class, auditable capacity contracts that express throughput guarantees, burst allowances, and provisioning windows. The existing autoscaler enforces SLA heuristics but lacks a declarative contract model and exposes minimal telemetry for burst accounting. This PR introduces a Policy-driven Capacity Contract model, integrates it with the autoscaler decision path, and ships a 'burst_accountant' telemetry subsystem to make overage and burst consumption visible in dashboards and billing exports.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a CapacityContract API (internal and CRD-backed operator model) that lets tenant operators declare: (a) guaranteed baseline throughput (tokens/sec), (b) burst budget (tokens and burst-window), (c) provisioning window (min lead time and headroom targets), and (d) priority class. The autoscaler is extended to consult active contracts when computing desired capacity and when evaluating soft-fallback policies. The burst_accountant component tracks burst consumption per-tenant and emits: burst.used, burst.remaining, burst.rate, burst.overage_events with HDR sketched percentiles for spike durations. Finally, this PR wires new contract-centric dashboards and a CSV exporter used by billing pipelines.

Design notes: - Contract evaluation is a pre-pass in the autoscaler: we compute contract-adjusted demand = max(observed_demand, contract.baseline). Contracts are weighted by priority class when conflict arises. - Soft fallback: when capacity is scarce, the autoscaler may temporarily honor contract priority but schedule a controlled degradation window (configurable percentage reduction) instead of outright eviction. - Burst accounting uses a leaky-bucket accumulator per-tenant with time-decayed credits; metrics are tagged with tenant_id, pool_id, and contract_id. - Operator safety: introducing a conservative rollout flag (feature_gate: capacityContracts=off by default in release configs). A migration helper converts existing reservation annotations into CapacityContract stubs for customers opting-in.

Implementation summary: - api/contracts/v1alpha1/types.go: CapacityContract schema and validation. - pkg/operator/contract_controller.go: controller that reconciles CRDs to internal cache. - pkg/autoscaler/contract_evaluator.go: integrates contract signals into scale decisions and fallback reasoning. - pkg/telemetry/burst_accountant/metrics.go + hdr sketch util: emits per-tenant burst metrics and aggregates. - dashboards/capacity_contracts.jsonnet: dashboard panels (burst budget panel, contract compliance over time). - tools/exporters/csv_burst_exporter.go: nightly CSV export for billing. - tests/integration/contract_autoscale_test.go and unit tests for the accountant.

Migration and rollout: - Default: feature gate off. Operators enabling the gate will be required to create a CapacityContract per-tenant or allow the migration helper to synthesize one. - Rollout strategy: phased canary by pool, 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days; monitor contract.compliance < 99% and burst.overage_events. - Backout: feature gate can be toggled off; autoscaler will revert to baseline heuristics.

Checklist:
- [x] API schema and validation
- [x] Autoscaler integration and safe fallbacks
- [x] Telemetry pipeline + HDR sketches
- [x] Dashboards and CSV exporter
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Docs: operator guide and migration notes

Related: This PR draws on previous autoscaling work but intentionally avoids touching the warm-pool allocator; it instead layers contracts as a higher-level admission filter. Related Linear items: ENG-4321 (capacity contracts RFC), ENG-7890 (burst telemetry backlog).

discussion:
Liam Nguyen (reviewer): Can we simplify the contract conflict resolution? The priority weighting logic seems likely to cause surprises when many tenants share a pool.

Aisha (author): We intentionally use a weighted allocation model so high-priority contracts get guaranteed baseline slices. I added more docs and unit tests to show examples and an RFC section illustrating deterministic outcomes. Open to making tie-breakers deterministic by contract creation timestamp — added as an optional rule.

Rory Kim (reviewer): CI integration tests failed on first run (race in accountant). Please add a shutdown sequence to flush sketches and close channels.

Aisha: Fixed in commit 0f3a99c; added a graceful shutdown test.

Sasha Iverson: Suggest exposing a sampled per-tenant contract.history metric to monitor frequent churn; otherwise approve.

Aisha: Added contract.history_count (sampled) and a panel to dashboards.

Rory Kim: Approved and merged after green CI.

CI notes: Initial runs: integration tests failed (flaky race). Flaky test addressed by additional sync in accountant.shutdown. Lint and unit tests passed. End-to-end perf benchmark (local) shows ~3% median latency impact on scale loop when gate enabled; we will gate this behind operator flag until rollout completes.
merge_outcome: merged via squash (merge commit message trimmed). Merged by Rory Kim on 2024-11-20. Merge method: squash and merge.
release_notes: - Introduce CapacityContract API and CRD for declaring baseline throughput, burst budgets, and provisioning windows. - Autoscaler now honors CapacityContracts and supports configurable soft-fallback degradations under contention. - New burst_accountant telemetry with burst.used, burst.remaining, burst.overage_events and HDR percentile exports. - Dashboards and CSV exporter for billing. Note: feature gate off by default; enable per-operator to opt-in.
migration_guide: Operators must enable the feature gate (capacityContracts=true) and either create CapacityContract CRs for tenants or run the migration helper that converts reservation annotations into contract stubs. Contracts default to conservative baselines to avoid unexpected capacity shifts. See docs/operator/capacity-contracts.md for step-by-step instructions.
